output.brief: The complaints most likely come from contaminated brake fluid, not from drivers, the new pads, or the hills. During the bay closure, Northfield changed the fluid in 13 Eastgate vans. Eleven of them used fluid from one old bulk drum that had a missing cap and had taken on water. The two vans that got fluid from a new drum have no complaints. All 11 complaining vans are among those 11 bulk-drum vans. When Northfield retested two of these vans on 24 Sep, the fluid boiled at about 150°C, against 255°C for sealed stock. Wet fluid can vaporise on long descents and make the pedal soft. Drivers who reported faults in the affected vans had no reports in other vans, including on Upper Wend, and Calder Road's vans fitted with Tessaro pads had no complaints. Do not discipline drivers or retrain everyone on this basis. Doing so would punish the people raising a real safety issue. This week: take the 11 bulk-drum vans off the road, test their fluid, and renew it from sealed stock. Also check the other two Northfield vans, and ask Calder Road for its fluid records. The pad supplier switch needs no action yet. I'm fairly confident, though the Calder fluid source and the wider noise reports remain unchecked.
